habitat: Dry bushveld and savanna woodland, where it is conspicuous. Two birds often call together with a wing-opening, head-bowing display.
summary: A common, near-endemic pied hornbill. The large yellow bill separates it from the other Kruger hornbills. The immature has a reddish base to the bill. The call works up to a crescendo and fades, wurk, wurk, wurk, wukwukak. The sexes are not separated in this account.

similar.note: Southern Red-billed Hornbill has a red bill and prefers drier ground, including mopane. Its call is similar but faster. Yellow-billed Hornbill has the large yellow bill.
African Grey Hornbill is darker grey, with a small dark or cream-and-red bill and a white eyebrow, not a large yellow bill.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^16=65536 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 32768–131072.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Pied. The texts do not name each head colour beyond the pied pattern and the yellow bill.

wings.pattern: Pied wings. A separate flight pattern was not named.

viewNotes.note: Large yellow bill on a pied bird in dry bushveld.
The yellow bill is the front mark.
Pied back. Part colours of the back were not named beyond pied.
Pied above. The upperwing pattern in flight was not named.
White underparts are implied by the pied pattern. The underwing was not named separately.

calls.description: wurk, wurk, wurk, wurk, wurk, wurk, wukwukak, wukwukak, working up to a crescendo and then fading. Often two birds call together. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Hammanskraal, Limpopo.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a common near-endemic resident. The photograph also shows a smaller bird, whose plumage was not copied into the marks because Newman only says the immature bill has a reddish base. Chick down beyond that, and a flight photograph, are gaps. The call is grade A from Limpopo.
